industry.size: Indian tyre industry revenue ~₹1.36 lakh cr in FY26; the top six makers are ~85% of it (CRISIL, 24-Aug-2026)
industry.fy26: Tyre industry grew an estimated 10% in FY26 and tyre exports 9% (MRF AR FY26 MD&A); CRISIL: volume +7-8%, operating margin ~14.2%
industry.fy27: CRISIL (24-Aug-2026): volume growth slows to 4-5% (replacement and OEM 4-5% each, exports 3-4%); key inputs up 35-40%; natural rubber ~₹275/kg in Jun-2026 vs ~₹220/kg in FY26; operating margin down 200-250 bp to ~11.5-12% in FY27, recovering to 13-13.5% in FY28 if input costs stabilise; 'a cost-pass-through lag rather than a structural profitability reset'; top six plan ~₹18,000 cr of capex over FY27-28, nearly double the previous two years
industry.rubber: Kottayam RSS-4 ₹27,300 per quintal (₹273/kg) on 3-Sep-2026; global futures ~240 US cents/kg on 1-Sep-2026, near the highest since 2013; 2026 output ~15.3 mn t vs demand ~15.4 mn t (Procurement Resource, 10-Sep-2026)
industry.priceHikes: Industry took 7-9% of price increases by Q1FY27 with more planned in Q2 (CLSA via Moneycontrol, 12-Aug-2026). Peers' Q4FY26 calls (Autocar Pro, 7-Jun-2026): Apollo 6-8% for Q1, CEAT ~5% in Mar-Apr plus 5% planned for May-Jun, JK 4-5% replacement plus 5-6% under way; RM up 15-20% q/q in Q1
industry.regulation: AIS-142 phase 2 (noise norms) from H2FY27 is expected to push OEMs off nylon truck tyres towards radials (MRF AR FY26); EPR for waste tyres; DGFT licensing of tyre imports since Jun-2020 limits Chinese imports (CARE)

excluded.TVSSRICHAK: Earnings distorted: FY25 EPS collapsed 81% to ₹26.9 (from ₹141) and its trailing P/E reached ~148x inside the five-year window; on 30-Sep-2026 it still trades on recovering earnings (ROE 6%)

peers.note: Listed Indian tyre makers with Screener data (PLAYBOOK §7c: full tyre set, MRF itself excluded). CEAT is kept: its peak P/E (~101x) came in the FY22 raw-material trough that hit the whole industry (MRF, Apollo and JK too), not from a company-specific one-off; a set without CEAT is shown as a sensitivity row.

brokers.thesis: Q1 margin 11.4% vs 12.6% est.; RM 67.3% of sales; 1% EPS CAGR FY26-28E; RoCE back to ~10%; 25.5x/21.9x FY27E/FY28E 'expensive' for subpar returns
Commodity headwinds (crude, rubber) weigh on margins; growth to track the industry; no case for a re-rating
Target raised from ₹1,39,000 (thesis not visible to us)
Margins to recover sequentially on 7-9% industry price increases, further hikes in Q2 and OEM cost pass-through
Q1FY26 miss; brighter margin outlook (FY25-28E: revenue +9%, EBITDA +13%, PAT +19% a year, Business Standard Dec-2025)

street.notUsed: Investing.com shows CLSA (₹165,238), Axis (₹143,000) and Kotak (₹124,000) actions dated 11-Nov-2026, after Q2FY27 and after our as-of date: not used. Univest blog 'targets' (YES Securities, JM Financial) are undated or unverified: not used.
street.consensus: No dated consensus EPS on or before 30-Sep-2026 was found; MOSL is the only post-Q1 note with a full estimate table.

ownership.src: BSE shareholding pattern for the quarter ended 30-Jun-2026 (via Trendlyne and Screener.in)

stockEvents: All-time high of ~₹1,60,190 (weekly close) after the GST 2.0 rate cuts
Low of ~₹1,23,420 after FY26 results and the Middle East-led rubber and crude spike
Q1FY27 results: margin 11.8%; the stock fell 2% (close ₹1,31,125), down 13.4% in 2026 to then
moat: 69% of sales from replacement through 5,000+ dealers; India's most recognised tyre brand; ~32% of industry units (CARE)
Truck-bus tyres are ~half of revenue; "definitive market leader" in two-wheeler tyres (AR FY26); 99 mn tyres of capacity; nine plants
No edge on raw material: margins move with rubber and crude like everyone's (10% in FY23, 17% in FY24); ROE 5-13% since FY21
Leads industry price increases, but with a lag of one to two quarters; OEM contracts pass costs through late
In-house technology, OE fitments on new EVs and 20-inch rims; but radialisation and premium PCR are areas where Apollo and CEAT are as strong
Chinese imports (capped by DGFT licensing), domestic capacity additions (~₹18,000 cr of industry capex), EV tyres
critiques: Returns are subpar: RoCE ~10-12% and ROE ~10-12%, so even 19-22x earnings is expensive.
Growth tracks the industry; commodity headwinds limit upside; no case for re-rating.
Price increases of 7-9% plus OEM pass-through should restore margins within a few quarters.
The squeeze is a cost-pass-through lag, not a structural reset; margins recover to 13-13.5% in FY28 if inputs stabilise.
Family directors' pay (~₹157 cr in FY26, up 45%) exceeds the total dividend (~₹100 cr); payout of ~4% keeps cash piling up at a ~6% yield.
The CCI cartel penalty of ₹622 cr (2011-12 conduct) is unprovided and still before the Supreme Court.

governance.auditor: M M Nissim & Co LLP and Sastri & Shah (joint auditors); unqualified opinion; key audit matter on litigation and contingent liabilities
governance.board: 14 directors, 7 independent, 3 women; five executive directors, all Mammen family members
governance.relatedParty: ₹322 cr of purchases from director-interested companies; ₹3,475 cr with subsidiaries (sourcing via MRF SG)
governance.capitalAllocation: Payout 4-5%; cash and liquid investments up from ₹5,169 cr to ₹7,572 cr in FY26; capex ₹1.3-1.4 kcr a year in FY25-26

gaps: MRF holds no earnings calls and publishes no investor presentation, so there is no management guidance on margins, capex or volumes; our forecasts rest on reported numbers, CARE, CRISIL and broker notes.
Channel mix is only available as rounded shares from CARE (FY24-FY26); MRF does not disclose volumes, realisations or product-level revenue.
Methods and multiples behind the Kotak, Axis Capital and CLSA targets were not visible to us (secondary sources only).
No dated consensus EPS on or before 30-Sep-2026.
Natural rubber price for late September 2026 not found; we use the 3-Sep-2026 Kottayam quote (₹273/kg).
The identity and control of Mowi Foundation (11.98%, the largest non-promoter holder) is not disclosed in the sources we read; we do not treat it as promoter-linked.

Q1FY27 standalone financials (beyond the MOSL table) and the Q1 press release were not read in the original; consolidated figures are Screener's, cross-checked with CARE (total operating income ₹8,610.6 cr incl. other income, PAT ₹495.35 cr).
conflicts: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin: 11.77% consolidated (Screener, Moneycontrol), 11.4% standalone (MOSL), 13.77% 'PBILDT' (CARE, which includes other income). We use 11.8% consolidated.
Q1FY27 PAT: ₹495.35 cr consolidated (CARE, Screener), ₹479.25 cr (Business Upturn) and ₹474 cr standalone (MOSL ₹4.7b). We use ₹495.35 cr.
FY26 other income: ₹504.6 cr reported vs ₹440 cr on Screener, which nets the ₹63.2 cr labour-code exceptional item.
Exports share: CARE says ~8% of channel sales; standalone exports of ₹2,324 cr are 7.6% of revenue. We use 7.6%.
Kotak's target: ₹125,000 (Business Upturn, 12-Aug-2026); Investing.com lists ₹125,000 only as the 'previous' target of a November action.
